Your data stays in that browser, and some features, such as website checks during scans, your own mailbox and an AI account of your own, need the Windows app. Today’s Windows download is a test version that hasn’t been tried on a real Windows machine yet.

chunks.title: FAQ (Email check): Is anything sent to the domain I check?
chunks.text:
Is anything sent to the domain I check?
No. The check only reads public DNS records, the same ones every mail server reads before it accepts an email. Your browser asks Cloudflare’s public DNS (Google Public DNS if Cloudflare doesn’t answer); no email is sent and no mailbox is touched. RadiusPilot receives nothing.

chunks.title: FAQ (Email check): Why does DKIM say “Unknown”?
chunks.text:
Why does DKIM say “Unknown”?
DNS can’t list a domain’s DKIM keys: you have to know a key’s name, its selector, to look it up. The check tries 22 names that common services use (google, selector1, k1…). A service that uses a custom name looks like “not found”, which is why the result is Unknown and not Missing. To be sure, open an email from the domain and read s= in its DKIM-Signature header.

chunks.title: FAQ (Email check): What’s a good DMARC policy?
chunks.text:
What’s a good DMARC policy?
Start with p=none and a reports address (rua=) to see who sends as the domain, fix the senders the reports show, then move to p=quarantine and later p=reject. p=none alone only watches: fake emails are still delivered.

chunks.title: FAQ (Email check): What is the SPF 10-lookup limit?
chunks.text:
What is the SPF 10-lookup limit?
Every include, a, mx, ptr, exists and redirect in an SPF record costs a DNS lookup, and the services it includes add theirs. Past 10, receivers stop and treat SPF as an error (a “permerror”), so the record protects nothing. The check counts the lookups in the record itself.

chunks.title: FAQ (Email check): Do Gmail and Yahoo require these records?
chunks.text:
Do Gmail and Yahoo require these records?
Yes, since February 2024: every sender needs SPF or DKIM, and bulk senders (around 5,000 messages a day to Gmail) need SPF, DKIM and DMARC, with a From domain that matches. Our guide to SPF, DKIM and DMARC (/guides/spf-dkim-dmarc-explained/) links to their pages.

chunks.title: FAQ (Email check): Can I share a result?
chunks.text:
Can I share a result?
Yes. After a check, the page’s address ends with ?domain= and the domain: anyone who opens it runs the same check again, with fresh records. Copy the results gives a plain-text summary to paste into an email or a note.

chunks.title: FAQ (Tools): Do the tools cost anything?
chunks.text:
Do the tools cost anything?
No. The website audit and the eight tools are part of every plan, Starter included, and the services they use need no account: Google PageSpeed, public DNS (Cloudflare, with Google as a backup) and the Internet Archive. Without a key, speed checks come from a daily limit Google shares among everyone, which often runs out. A PageSpeed key from your own Google account costs nothing and gives 25,000 checks a day.

chunks.title: FAQ (Tools): Why do some tools need the Windows app?
chunks.text:
Why do some tools need the Windows app?
Site technology, Published contacts, the Brand kit tool’s “From a website” and the audit’s read of the site itself all read another website’s pages. A web page isn’t allowed to read other sites, so the Windows app reads them from your computer, one site at a time, when you ask.

chunks.title: FAQ (Tools): Is Published contacts a scraper?
chunks.text:
Is Published contacts a scraper?
No. It reads one business’s own website at your request, the homepage and up to five of its contact, team, about or legal pages, and shows what that business publishes about reaching it, with the page each item is on. It never guesses addresses, never decodes addresses hidden from robots, never searches other websites and keeps no list of what it found.

chunks.title: FAQ (Tools): Can I check the demo businesses?
chunks.text:
Can I check the demo businesses?
No. Demo businesses have invented websites and phone numbers that may belong to someone else, so the checks only work on real businesses, from your scans or your own file, or on an address you type. A demo business’s audit is generated from its demo data, and nothing is checked.

chunks.title: FAQ (Tools): Does Email health send anything?
chunks.text:
Does Email health send anything?
No. It only reads the domain’s public DNS records: MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC. When a record is missing it suggests a starter record you can share with the business.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): Are payments live?
chunks.text:
Are payments live?
Not yet. RadiusPilot doesn’t take payments today. In the app, choosing a plan or buying credits is simulated: you get the plan’s limits and credits on your computer and a simulated invoice marked “no payment was taken”. No card is charged.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): What currency are the prices in?
chunks.text:
What currency are the prices in?
US dollars, per month, before taxes. Yearly billing takes 17% off the monthly price.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): What are credits?
chunks.text:
What are credits?
The one unit for what costs RadiusPilot money each time it runs: Verify listing, RadiusPilot AI, scans past your plan’s and the API (/developers/). Most tasks use 1 to 3 credits, a scan 10. Scans within your plan, imports, exports and the tools use none.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): What happens when I run out?
chunks.text:
What happens when I run out?
The action stops before it starts and says so, with two ways out: buy credits, or, for AI, connect your own AI in Settings › AI. Nothing is charged automatically, and nothing pops up in the background.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): Do credits roll over?
chunks.text:
Do credits roll over?
Your plan’s credits renew on its renewal date and don’t roll over. Credits you buy last 12 months. Your plan’s credits are spent first, then bought ones, oldest first, and a failed action gives its credits back.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): Is pay as you go cheaper than Pro?
chunks.text:
Is pay as you go cheaper than Pro?
Only for light use. Pay as you go costs $0.22 to $0.29 a credit, top-ups $0.09 to $0.12. Past about 400 credits a month, Pro costs less: its 25 scans and 300 credits are worth 550 credits, about $137 pay as you go, for $99.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): What counts as a scan?
chunks.text:
What counts as a scan?
Each real scan of one area counts as one, whatever the number of kinds of businesses, and scanning an area again is a new scan. A scan that fails or finds nothing gives its scan back, and Starter’s preview scan isn’t used up, so you can try again. Past your plan’s scans, a scan uses 10 credits.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): What does Starter’s real scan show?
chunks.text:
What does Starter’s real scan show?
How many real businesses it found, how many are high opportunity, and up to three of them. Their phone numbers and websites, and the rest of the list, open on a paid plan or with a scan paid in credits.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): Can I pick how many scans I get?
chunks.text:
Can I pick how many scans I get?
Yes. Pro comes with 25, 50 or 100 scans and 300, 600 or 1,200 credits a month, Agency with 100, 250 or 500 scans and 1,000, 2,000 or 4,000 credits. You choose the volume with the plan.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): What does a plan change in the app?
chunks.text:
What does a plan change in the app?
Five things: the real scans a month, the businesses per scan, the credits it includes and the price of more, the seats, and white-label on Agency. Nothing else is counted or locked by plan today: reports, pitch decks, lead lists, PDF export, the pipeline, clients and projects work on every plan.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): Do the tools or AI cost extra?
chunks.text:
Do the tools or AI cost extra?
The website audit and the eight tools are part of every plan and use no credits. RadiusPilot AI is included, in the web app and the Windows app: each task uses 1 to 5 credits. AI of your own uses none: in the Windows app, Codex or Continue with ChatGPT use your ChatGPT plan, and an OpenAI API key is billed by OpenAI. RadiusPilot charges nothing for either.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): Is there an API?
chunks.text:
Is there an API?
Yes, in beta. The RadiusPilot API (/developers/) searches an area’s businesses with their scores, checks a website and drafts outreach with RadiusPilot AI, billed in the same credits. It opens to accepted beta testers (/beta/) first, each with 50 credits to try it.

chunks.title: FAQ (Pricing): What do “Planned” and “Beta” mean?
chunks.text:
What do “Planned” and “Beta” mean?
“Planned” is announced in the app’s plan sheet, where it says Soon, and not built yet: competitor intelligence, CRM sync, custom domains, priority scanning and webhooks. Each one moves to the changelog when it ships. “Beta” is the website builder and its editor, and the API: open to beta testers (/beta/) first, on any plan.

chunks.title: FAQ (Download): What does it cost?
chunks.text:
What does it cost?
Starter is $0 a month: one real scan as a preview, your own lists from a CSV file and every tool. Payments aren’t live yet: choosing a paid plan in the app is simulated and charges nothing.

chunks.title: FAQ (Download): Do I need an account?
chunks.text:
Do I need an account?
Not for the app: you create its account on your computer. An account on this website, for support tickets, is optional.

chunks.title: FAQ (Download): Does it update itself?
chunks.text:
Does it update itself?
Not yet. New versions are listed in the changelog, and you download them from this page.

chunks.title: FAQ (Download): Is there a Mac or Linux version?
chunks.text:
Is there a Mac or Linux version?
Not as a download. On a Mac, Linux, a Chromebook or any other computer, the web app (/web/) runs RadiusPilot in a modern browser, with your data kept in that browser. Website checks during scans, Site technology, Published contacts, sending from your mailbox and an AI account of your own need the Windows app; RadiusPilot AI works in both.

chunks.title: FAQ (Download): Can I try it without installing anything?
chunks.text:
Can I try it without installing anything?
Yes. The web app (/web/) runs in your browser with your own account and workspaces, and the live demo (/demo/) opens the demo workspace. You can move your work to the Windows app later with a backup.

chunks.title: FAQ (Download): Can I use it on my phone?
chunks.text:
Can I use it on my phone?
No. RadiusPilot is made for a computer screen, in the Windows app or the web app. Open this page on your PC to download it.

chunks.title: FAQ (Beta access): Who gets in first?
chunks.text:
Who gets in first?
Agencies and freelancers who sell websites and marketing to local businesses, starting in Québec and the rest of Canada. Your team, your clients, how you heard about RadiusPilot and a clear plan for what you’d build count too.

chunks.title: FAQ (Beta access): How is my request reviewed?
chunks.text:
How is my request reviewed?
RadiusPilot AI, an automated assistant, reads it and decides between access now and the waitlist, using only what the form asks. It gives access at once only when a request clearly fits and a seat is still open. Otherwise you join the waitlist, ordered by fit, then by date. If the assistant can’t answer, a person reviews your request.

chunks.title: FAQ (Beta access): Can a person look at the decision?
chunks.text:
Can a person look at the decision?
Yes. Ask for a person to review it, or to correct what you sent, from the contact form (/support/?topic=support#contact). Say “beta request” in your message.

chunks.title: FAQ (Beta access): How do I use my beta code?
chunks.text:
How do I use my beta code?
In the RadiusPilot app, open the website builder and choose I have a beta code, then paste it. Keep it to yourself: it’s tied to your request.

chunks.title: FAQ (Beta access): Does the beta include the API?
chunks.text:
Does the beta include the API?
Yes. Accepted beta testers can create keys for the RadiusPilot API (/developers/) on their account (/account/#api), with 50 credits to try it. Paste your beta code with your first key.

chunks.title: FAQ (Beta access): What do you keep about my request?
chunks.text:
What do you keep about my request?
Your answers to the form, the assistant’s score, decision and reasons, and a keyed hash of your IP address that limits repeated requests. We keep them until 12 months after the beta ends, or until you ask us to delete them. See the privacy policy (/privacy/#beta).

chunks.title: FAQ (Beta access): I lost my private link
chunks.text:
I lost my private link
Write to us from the contact form (/support/?topic=support#contact), from the address you applied with, and say “beta request” in your message. We’ll tell you where your request stands.

chunks.title: Tool: Site speed
chunks.text:
Site speed: Google’s speed, accessibility and SEO scores for any website, on a phone or a computer.
Uses: Google PageSpeed.
What a check gives:
- Four Lighthouse scores
- Lab timings, and real-visitor data when Google has it
- Google’s list of fixes and a screenshot
- About 15 to 40 seconds a check
Show a business how its homepage loads on a phone, with Google’s own numbers.

chunks.title: Tool: Email health
chunks.text:
Email health: The records that keep a domain’s email out of spam and stop others faking it.
Uses: Public DNS.
What a check gives:
- MX: who handles the mail
- SPF: the senders allowed, the lookups used
- DKIM: 22 common selectors, unknown when not found
- DMARC: the policy, with starter records to suggest
Nothing is sent: it only reads public DNS records.

chunks.title: Tool: Site technology
chunks.text:
Site technology: The builder, booking tool, analytics and plugins behind a homepage, and what’s out of date.
Uses: Reads the homepage. Windows app only.
What a check gives:
- About 130 technologies, each with its clue
- Old analytics, jQuery, PHP or WordPress
- No HTTPS, no mobile viewport, an old copyright year
- Header and cookie names only, never their values
Know what a site runs on before the first call.

chunks.title: Tool: Published contacts
chunks.text:
Published contacts: The emails, phones, address, form and social links a business publishes on its own site, each with its page.
Uses: Reads the business’s site. Windows app only.
What a check gives:
- The homepage and up to five contact, team, about or legal pages
- Role or personal-looking addresses, named only when the site names them
- A page that refuses unsolicited messages blocks saving
- Saves one role address of the site’s own domain, with its page
It never guesses addresses, never decodes the ones a site hides from robots and never searches other websites.

chunks.title: Tool: Site history
chunks.text:
Site history: When the Internet Archive first saved a website, and when its homepage last changed.
Uses: Internet Archive.
What a check gives:
- First and last saved copies
- The last real change
- Changes per year
- A link to each year’s last copy
A homepage untouched since 2019 is a good reason to call.

chunks.title: Tool: QR codes
chunks.text:
QR codes: QR codes for a website, a phone, an email or Wi-Fi, in the business’s colours.
Uses: On your computer.
What a check gives:
- Website, phone, email, Wi-Fi or text
- Square, rounded or dot styles, with a logo
- A warning when the contrast is too low
- PNG or SVG; the Wi-Fi password is never saved
A leave-behind for the counter, made in a minute.

chunks.title: Tool: Brand kit
chunks.text:
Brand kit: A business’s colours, readable text pairs and fonts, from its logo or its website.
Uses: On your computer.
What a check gives:
- From a logo file, or the site’s own styles in the Windows app
- Text and background pairs that pass WCAG contrast
- The site’s fonts, or a pairing suggested for the business
- CSS and design tokens (JSON); saved on the business, it colours its posts and QR codes
Mockups, posts and reports in the client’s own colours.

chunks.title: Tool: Post maker
chunks.text:
Post maker: Social posts filled from a business’s details and brand kit, sized for Instagram, Stories and Facebook.
Uses: On your computer.
What a check gives:
- Announcement, offer, hours, event and tip layouts
- Square, portrait, Story and wide sizes, saved as PNG
- Fills in a business’s name, contact, hours and brand kit
- Write it with AI, labelled AI-generated
A ready post to attach to the first email.

chunks.title: Email check: Check a domain’s email setup

Check a domain’s email setup
MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC in a few seconds. See whether a business can receive email, and whether anyone can fake it.
Email check
Public DNS records only, read from your browser. Nothing is sent to the domain or kept by us.
- MX: Receives email: Whether the domain can receive email, and which service handles it.
- SPF: Allowed senders: Which servers may send email for the domain.
- DKIM: Signed email: Whether outgoing email is signed, so it can’t be changed on the way.
- DMARC: Protection from fakes: What receivers should do with email that fakes the domain.

chunks.title: Email check › Four records, one answer
chunks.text:
Each one answers a question a mail server asks before it trusts an email.
- MX: where email goes: Mail exchanger records name the servers that receive the domain’s email. Without one, email sent to the business bounces. A “null MX” says on purpose that the domain takes no email.
- SPF: who may send: One TXT record on the domain lists the servers allowed to send its email, and ends with what to do with the others: ~all marks them as suspicious, -all fails them. Only one SPF record is allowed, within 10 DNS lookups.
- DKIM: a signature on each email: The sending service signs each message; receivers check it with a public key published at selector._domainkey. DNS can’t list selectors, so a key under a custom name doesn’t show up here.
- DMARC: what to do with fakes: A TXT record at _dmarc tells receivers what to do with email that fails SPF and DKIM for the domain: nothing (p=none), spam (quarantine) or refuse it (reject), and where to send reports.

chunks.title: Developers: The RadiusPilot API
chunks.text:
The RadiusPilot API
Search an area’s businesses with their opportunity scores, check a website and draft outreach with RadiusPilot AI, from your own code. Billed in credits, in beta.
Overview
The API gives your code what a scan gives you in the app: the businesses of an area with their opportunity scores, a read of a website, and drafts and reports from RadiusPilot AI. It takes and answers JSON, over HTTPS, at one address:
Base URL · https://radiuspilot.com/api/v1/
Opening soon, in beta: The API opens to accepted beta testers first. Each accepted account gets 50 credits to try it, once. Payments aren’t live yet, so more credits can’t be bought yet. Fields may be added during the beta; changes are announced in the changelog (/changelog/).
- Credits: 50 to try it, from the same balance as the app
- Limits: 30 requests a minute and 1,000 a day, per key
- Version: v1, in the address

chunks.title: Developers › Get a key
chunks.text:
- Join the beta: Request access on the beta page (/beta/). An accepted request comes with a beta code.
- Create a key: Sign in to your account (/account/#api), open API and choose Create key. Name it after where it will run. The first time, paste your beta code.
- Copy it once: The key is shown once. Keep it in your server’s secrets or a password manager: we store only a hash of it and its first 12 characters, so we can’t show it again.
- Revoke it any time: On the same page. It stops working at once, and the apps using it with it.
Keep keys on your server: A key spends your credits. Never put one in a web page, an app people download or a public repository. Revoke it if it leaks.

chunks.title: Developers › Authentication
chunks.text:
Send your key in the Authorization header of every request. Keys start with rp_live_, then 32 random characters.
A missing, mistyped or revoked key gets 401 unauthorized. Every answer carries an X-Request-Id header: quote it when you write to us about a request.

chunks.title: Developers › Credits
chunks.text:
Requests spend credits from your account’s balance, the same credits as in the app. A success says what it used and what’s left, in credits:
Endpoint | Credits:
- GET /v1/account (/developers/#ep-account): 0
- POST /v1/businesses/search (/developers/#ep-search): 10
- POST /v1/sites/check (/developers/#ep-site): 1
- POST /v1/ai/write (/developers/#ep-write): 1
- POST /v1/ai/report (/developers/#ep-report): 3
- A request that fails gives its credits back: a server error, or a service behind it that doesn’t answer.
- Without enough credits, a request answers 402 not_enough_credits and spends nothing. Nothing is ever charged automatically.
- What each action costs in the app, and the credit packs, are on the pricing page (/pricing/#credits).

chunks.text: Five endpoints in v1. Paths are relative to the base URL. Requests with a body send JSON with Content-Type: application/json.

chunks.text:

chunks.title: Developers › POST /v1/businesses/search
chunks.text:
POST · /v1/businesses/search · 10 credits
Businesses in an area, scored. Every named business of the kinds you ask for around a point, nearest first, each with its opportunity score from 0 to 100 and the reasons behind it: the same facts and weights as a scan in the app.
Body | Type | What it is:
- lat | number | Required. Latitude of the centre, like 45.5231
- lng | number | Required. Longitude of the centre, like -73.5817
- radius_m | integer | Required. The radius in metres, from 100 to 5,000
- categories | string[] | Optional. Kinds of businesses: dentist, restaurant, cafe, gym, salon, spa, auto, plumber, hvac, roofing, law, realestate, vet, clinic, chiro, bakery, retail, hotel. Leave it out for all 18
- limit | integer | Optional. At most 500 businesses
In the answer | Type | What it is:
- score | integer | 0 to 100: the higher, the more the business is missing that an agency can fix
- level | string | "high" (60 and up), "medium" (40 to 59) or "low"
- reasons | string[] | What the score is built from, in words
- attribution | string | The data licence’s credit: show it with the data (below)

chunks.title: Developers › POST /v1/sites/check
chunks.text:
POST · /v1/sites/check · 1 credit
Check a website. One ordinary request for a homepage, as a browser makes it: where it lands, whether it loads over HTTPS and fits a phone, its title and description, online booking, the technology behind it and its social links.
Body | Type | What it is:
- url | string | Required. The website, like https://maplefitness.example.com

chunks.title: Developers › POST /v1/ai/write
chunks.text:
POST · /v1/ai/write · 1 credit
Draft an email or a message. RadiusPilot AI drafts a first email, a follow-up or a short message to a business, from the facts you give it. It writes; it never sends.
Body | Type | What it is:
- business | object | Required. name, and optionally category, city and facts (short sentences it may use)
- kind | string | Required. "email", "follow_up" or "message"
- language | string | Optional. A language code, like "en" or "fr"
- notes | string | Optional. What you sell, the tone, what to mention

chunks.title: Developers › POST /v1/ai/report
chunks.text:
POST · /v1/ai/report · 3 credits
Write a report. RadiusPilot AI writes a short report in Markdown: a website review from its URL, or a business’s situation from the facts you send.
Body | Type | What it is:
- business | object | Optional. As for ai/write
- url | string | Optional. A website to review
- facts | string[] | Optional. Facts to build on
- language | string | Optional. A language code, like "en" or "fr"

chunks.title: Developers › Errors
chunks.text:
An error has an HTTP status and a body with a short code to test against and a message to read:
Status | Code | What happened:
- 400 | invalid_request | A field is missing, has the wrong type or is out of range
- 401 | unauthorized | No key, a mistyped key or a revoked one
- 402 | not_enough_credits | The request needs more credits than are left. Nothing is spent
- 403 | beta_only | The account isn’t an accepted beta tester yet
- 404 | not_found | No such endpoint
- 429 | rate_limited | Over the key’s limit. Retry-After says how many seconds to wait
- 502 | upstream_failed | A service behind the request didn’t answer. Its credits are given back
- 503 | server_busy | A daily limit on our side is reached. Try again later
- 503 | not_configured | That part of the API isn’t switched on yet

chunks.title: Developers › Limits
chunks.text:
- 30 requests a minute and 1,000 a day, per key. Past either one: 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After in seconds.
- RadiusPilot AI keeps its own daily limits on our server. When one is reached, ai/write and ai/report answer 503 server_busy until later.
- During the beta, business searches also share a daily cap across every key. Past it, businesses/search answers 503 server_busy.
- Credits a busy or failed request didn’t use stay on your balance.

chunks.title: Developers › What it never returns
chunks.text:
- Google data. Google’s terms don’t allow passing it on, so Verify listing stays in the app.
- Email addresses. Collecting addresses in bulk with software goes against Canada’s anti-spam and privacy laws, so the API never does it.
- What a site hides from robots. A site check reads the homepage as a visitor sees it, and never decodes a hidden address.
- Ratings, reviews or rankings. Public listings don’t have them, and RadiusPilot never makes them up.

chunks.title: Developers › The data licence
chunks.text:
Business data comes from public listings shared under an open licence, which asks for a credit wherever the data is shown. Every search answer carries it in attribution. Show it next to the data, as RadiusPilot’s exported reports do.
Read the licence and how to give the credit

chunks.title: Developers › Drafts and anti-spam law
chunks.text:
ai/write writes a draft. It never sends anything, and what you send is up to you:
- Email a business only with its consent, express or implied, as Canada’s anti-spam law (CASL) asks for email received in Canada.
- Add your business name, your postal address and a working way to unsubscribe. RadiusPilot’s own outreach adds them for you; a draft from the API doesn’t.
- Read it before it goes out: it’s AI-generated and can be wrong.
See Email rules (/help/email-rules/#casl) and the CASL guide (/guides/casl-cold-email-canada/). Not legal advice.

- OpenAI, only if you set up your own AI: Through your own Codex, ChatGPT or API account: what you ask it to write, with the facts it needs about that business, offer or market, and, unless you switch background analysis off, real businesses’ facts up to your daily cap

chunks.title: Privacy policy (draft) › The app (part 5 of 5)
chunks.text:
RadiusPilot AI is included in the web app and the Windows app. When you ask it to write, what you asked and the facts it needs go to our server, which asks Claude, an AI model by Anthropic (United States), to write the answer, under Anthropic’s privacy policy. We don’t keep what you asked or the answer: only how much each connection used each day, keyed by a hash of its IP address, never the address itself, so the daily allowance is shared fairly.
Scans and listing checks go through our server, which asks Google Places, under Google’s privacy policy: the area and kinds of businesses of a scan, or a business’s name, address and location. What Google returns about businesses is saved in your workspace, on your device, like any scan result. Our server doesn’t keep it: only a count per connection.
Your own AI is optional. If you set it up in the Windows app, requests go to OpenAI, outside Québec, under your own OpenAI or ChatGPT account and OpenAI’s policies, not through us.
The app has no analytics, no tracking and no crash reporting.

chunks.title: Privacy policy (draft) › Information about businesses and the people who run them
chunks.text:
Real scans list businesses from Google Places, through our server, as described above. The Published contacts tool shows only what a business publishes on its own website, one business at a time and at your request, with the page each item comes from. It doesn’t guess addresses or decode hidden ones. It keeps only an address you choose to use as a business’s email, with the page it came from.
Businesses, prospects and clients you import from your own CSV file stay on your device. You confirm that you’re allowed to email the addresses in it, or leave them out.
You decide what you do with that information, and you’re responsible for following the law when you contact anyone, including Canada’s anti-spam law (CASL) and private-sector privacy laws.

chunks.title: Privacy policy (draft) › Email
chunks.text: When you connect your mailbox in the app, your email travels between the app and your mail provider. We don’t see it. Every outreach email carries your mailing address and a way to opt out, and the addresses on your opt-out list are blocked.

chunks.title: Privacy policy (draft) › Your rights
chunks.text:
You can ask to access the personal information we hold about you, to correct it, to withdraw your consent, to have it deleted, or to receive it in a structured, commonly used format.
Signed in, you can do most of this yourself: correct your profile in Settings, download your data with Export my data, and remove everything with Delete my account.
For anything else, send a privacy request from the Support page (/support/#contact), or write to <email address>. We’ll answer within 30 days.
When a decision about you is made only by automated means, such as the review of a beta request (/privacy/#beta), you can ask what personal information was used, the reasons and main factors behind the decision, and for a person to review it.
You can also complain to the Commission d’accès à l’information du Québec or to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.
